survey: An upright wooden coffin standing on its narrow foot end on grass, seen at three-quarter view. Main parts: (1) the front lid, a six-sided coffin shape with a raised light-wood cross attached flat to its face; (2) the box body behind it, whose right side wall shows as a separate tall six-sided panel with matching angled edges; (3) a purple quilted lining visible in a vertical gap between the lid's right edge and the side wall; (4) a flat top surface across the head end. The lid looks pushed slightly open on the right. Its left edge sits flush with the body and no hinge is shown. The foot end rests on the grass with a contact shadow, and the widest point (the shoulder) is near the top, which suits a coffin standing upright.

errors.where: Head end (top) of the coffin, where the lid meets the right side wall
errors.what: The lid stands open along its whole right edge, showing a gap with lining from shoulder to foot. Yet at the top, a single flat top surface runs straight across the lid and the gap and joins the side wall. An opened lid cannot stay joined to the box at the top; the lid and body merge there. The six-sided taper of the lid is also not carried into this top surface, which reads as a flat, near-rectangular slab.

errors.where: Left long edge of the lid and the gap on the right
errors.what: The lid is shown open by an even, door-like gap with no hinge, latch or pivot. The left edge is flush and seamless with the body, so nothing explains how the lid opens or what holds it in this half-open position.

errors.where: Foot end, bottom of the gap
errors.what: At the bottom, the gap narrows and the lid edge melts into the side wall instead of meeting it at a clear seam or corner.

fix: Upright wooden coffin with a separate six-sided lid, slightly ajar: the lid swings out on visible metal hinges along its left edge, and its right edge stands clear of the box from head to foot. Show a clean, even gap at the top and the bottom, with the purple quilted lining visible inside the open edge. The box has its own six-sided rim at the head end that matches the lid's outline. The lid and box are clearly two pieces and do not merge at the top or bottom.
